structured_output.what_is_happening: NEVER ("Never Kill Yourself") is a pump.fun coin about 10 minutes old, still on the bonding curve, with a market cap of about $15.6k. Its X link is a post from @MostGentleDev (I could not fetch it: HTTP 402), its website is a UsePaid token page (fetch failed with an SSL error), and its description says fees go to the 988 Lifeline via UsePaid. According to GMGN it is up about 4x from launch but already about 55% below its ATH (ATH price 3.44e-5 vs 1.56e-5 now, about $34k ATH market cap). The last 5 minutes are busy: 338 buys vs 216 sells and $18k of volume. GMGN flags 110 bundler wallets, a top bundler trader share of 30%, and a bot/degen rate of 36%. The same meme name has been launched over and over: the packet lists at least 8 other "Never Kill Yourself" tokens, and nearly all of them died around $3.4k.

narrative.description: An evergreen, wholesome anti-suicide meme ('never kill yourself', documented by KnowYourMeme and the Daily Dot) with a charity hook: creator fees go to the 988 Lifeline through UsePaid.
narrative.why_spreading: I found no current event or catalyst. It looks like a recurring meme relaunch, and the charity-fee angle gives it some novelty. Attention is probably coming from pump.fun front-page and bot traders, not from outside discussion.

token_connection.why_this_token: This one currently has by far the most volume and a DexScreener profile that points to a charity-fee post. Most same-name clones are dead.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 8 other 'Never Kill Yourself'/NEVER tokens, including Ct9kK4... launched minutes earlier with $10k h1 volume, plus 2xaWUR..., Ap4pfT... and others near $3k market cap.

authenticity.evidence: GMGN counts 110 bundler wallets, a 30% top bundler trader share and a 36% bot/degen rate. There are also 375 unique buyers per GeckoTerminal, 7 smart wallets, no snipers and no paid DexScreener boosts. I found no organic X, Reddit or news discussion of this contract.
authenticity.uncertainty: I could not read the X post or the UsePaid page, so I can't see how big the post's reach is.
